why_now: audit-l06-b4-gnum-guard-20260912T005926 and lnum-blocker-c9f0dc897f5293a44329 both record that the guard still reports contest=true at 1e6cdf04d7a2, and name the remedy as 'a controller disposition or guard supersession rule'. method: Load the hash-pinned copy of numerics/gates.py (bytecode writing disabled); run its _protocol_review over a snapshot of research_map/events.jsonl (arm A0). For each synthetic channel event type (A1-A8) append exactly one event to the snapshot and re-run the live predicate. Then run shadow_review (prior task's extracted rule hook implementation) with hooks off (equivalence control E1), scope-only (B1), scope+withdrawal (B2), scope+withdrawal+discharge (B3) against a synthetic structured withdrawal and a synthetic discharge carrier, and the six negative controls from the prior task plus the discharge-carrier controls.

preregistered_expectations.claim: shadow_review with all hooks off reproduces the pinned live _protocol_review output exactly on the A0 snapshot (same reviewed flag, same accept ids, same dissent ids, same contest, same advisory count).

No single live-predicate channel arm (A1 status disposition, A2 gate pass verdict, A3 gate discharge list, A4 review rebind of the r4 accept, A5 review carrying discharges[], A6 artifact disposition record, A7 astra structured withdrawal, A8 dissent-author structured withdrawal) yields contest=false. A4/A5 may raise the counted accept count; contest stays true in every channel arm.

Shadow scope-only (R1) leaves contest=true; scope+withdrawal (R1+R2) leaves contest=true at the frozen stream (no structured withdrawal exists live) and clears only when the synthetic author withdrawal A8 is present; R1+R2+R3 with the synthetic discharge carrier yields contest=false.
All six negative controls on R1+R2+R3 fail closed (contest=true): unknown discharge id, stale-hash carrier, pre-dated carrier, uncited carrier, third-party withdrawal, fresh unlisted dissent.
The two live pins are byte-identical before and after the measurement window.

stop_rules: Exit 2 if either live pin moves during the window (measurement voids, finding stands).
Exit 3 if any preregistered expectation is falsified.
Exit 4 if a negative control clears contest (fail-open rule is unsafe; do not propose adoption).
non_claims: no modification of numerics/gates.py or any canonical file
no claim outside the pinned snapshot bytes
the synthetic channel events are simulations, not emitted protocol events
falsifier: Any single channel arm yielding contest=false under the live predicate, or any negative control clearing contest under the shadow rule, or a live-pin move, falsifies the corresponding expectation.
